svg.title: One word, two tastes: the Greek compound for bitter-sweet
svg.desc: Sappho's compound adjective γλυκύπικρον (Wharton fr. 40, Voigt 130) split into its two halves, γλυκύς 'sweet' and πικρός 'bitter' (LSJ). Below, Wharton's prose and Symonds' verse both write 'bitter-sweet', the halves in reverse order, and the Nobel Committee's sentence that her essay Eros the Bittersweet draws on a compound adjective from Sappho (the Committee does not name the word). Educational demos made to show an open-source tool. Not research.
